title: No row was found for FETCH, UPDATE or DELETE, or the query result is empty
cause: The statement ran correctly but its WHERE clause matched no rows, or a cursor reached the end of its result set.
fix: Treat it as end-of-data, not a failure. If rows were expected, check the predicate values, trailing blanks in CHAR columns and the current schema.

title: The string constant is not terminated
cause: A quote that opens a string literal has no matching closing quote, often because the text itself contains an apostrophe.
fix: Close the literal and double any apostrophe inside it, or better, pass the value as a parameter marker instead of building the SQL string.

title: An unexpected token was found in the SQL statement
cause: Syntax error: a keyword, comma or parenthesis is missing or misplaced, or a statement terminator was sent as part of the statement.
fix: Read the token named in the message and the text just before it. Remove a trailing semicolon when executing through a driver, and check for reserved words used as names.

title: The number of values assigned is not the same as the number of specified or implied columns
cause: An INSERT supplies more or fewer values than the column list (or the table) has columns.
fix: List the target columns explicitly in the INSERT and supply exactly one value per column.
example_sql: SELECT COLNAME, COLNO FROM SYSCAT.COLUMNS WHERE TABNAME = ? ORDER BY COLNO

title: A column in the SELECT, HAVING or ORDER BY clause is not in the GROUP BY clause
cause: A non-aggregated column is selected alongside aggregate functions without being grouped.
fix: Add the column to GROUP BY, or wrap it in an aggregate such as MAX() or MIN().

title: The syntax of the string representation of a datetime value is incorrect
cause: A string could not be parsed as DATE, TIME or TIMESTAMP because its format is not one Db2 recognises.
fix: Use ISO formats (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) or convert explicitly with TO_DATE / TIMESTAMP_FORMAT and a format string.

title: The string representation of a datetime value is out of range
cause: The string has a valid format but an impossible value, such as month 13 or 30 February.
fix: Validate dates in the application before sending them, and check for day/month order mix-ups.

title: A reference to a column is ambiguous
cause: The same column name exists in more than one table of the FROM clause and is used without a qualifier.
fix: Qualify the column with its table name or correlation name (o.ID instead of ID).

title: The object name is undefined
cause: The table, view, alias or other object does not exist in the schema Db2 looked in. Unqualified names resolve to CURRENT SCHEMA, which defaults to the connected user ID.
fix: Qualify the name with its schema, or run SET CURRENT SCHEMA. Check spelling and case: names created inside double quotes are case-sensitive. Confirm you are connected to the right database.
example_sql: SELECT TABSCHEMA, TABNAME FROM SYSCAT.TABLES WHERE TABNAME = ?

title: The column name is not valid in the context where it is used
cause: The column does not exist in the referenced tables, is misspelled, or a string literal was written in double quotes so Db2 read it as a column name.
fix: Check the column name against the catalog. Use single quotes for string values; double quotes are for identifiers.
example_sql: SELECT COLNAME FROM SYSCAT.COLUMNS WHERE TABSCHEMA = ? AND TABNAME = ?

title: A default table space could not be found with a sufficient page size
cause: The table's row size or column count needs a larger page size than any USER table space the authorization ID may use.
fix: Create a buffer pool and a table space with an 8K, 16K or 32K page size and grant USE on it, or reduce the row width.

title: Unable to allocate new pages in the table space
cause: The table space is full: its containers, storage paths or maximum size are exhausted.
fix: Free disk space, add a storage path or container, or raise MAXSIZE / enable AUTORESIZE for the table space.

title: The value of a host variable or parameter is too large for its use
cause: A bound input value is longer or larger than the target column or parameter type allows.
fix: Validate the length in the application, or widen the column or parameter type.

title: Assignment of a NULL value to a NOT NULL column is not allowed
cause: An INSERT or UPDATE sets a NOT NULL column to NULL, usually because the column was omitted and has no default.
fix: Supply a value, add a DEFAULT to the column, or drop the NOT NULL constraint if nulls are valid. The message gives TBSPACEID, TABLEID and COLNO to identify the column.
example_sql: SELECT C.TABNAME, C.COLNAME FROM SYSCAT.COLUMNS C JOIN SYSCAT.TABLES T ON T.TABSCHEMA = C.TABSCHEMA AND T.TABNAME = C.TABNAME WHERE T.TBSPACEID = ? AND T.TABLEID = ? AND C.COLNO = ?

title: A value is not compatible with the data type of its assignment target
cause: The source value's type cannot be assigned to the target column, for example a character string into an INTEGER column.
fix: CAST the value to the target type or fix the application's parameter binding type.

title: Invalid character found in a character string argument of a function
cause: A string being converted to a number contains characters that are not part of a valid numeric value.
fix: Clean the data before casting, and find the offending rows with a pattern test before converting the column.

title: The value is too long
cause: A string is longer than the target column, variable or function result allows and Db2 will not truncate it silently.
fix: Shorten the value, widen the column with ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE, or truncate deliberately with SUBSTR or LEFT.

title: No authorized routine of the given name with compatible arguments was found
cause: The function or procedure does not exist in the SQL path, the argument count or types do not match any signature, or EXECUTE privilege is missing.
fix: Check the routine name, schema and argument types; CAST arguments to the declared types; grant EXECUTE if needed.
example_sql: SELECT ROUTINESCHEMA, ROUTINENAME, SPECIFICNAME FROM SYSCAT.ROUTINES WHERE ROUTINENAME = ?

title: The insert or update value of a foreign key is not equal to any value of the parent key
cause: A child row references a parent key value that does not exist in the parent table.
fix: Insert the parent row first, or correct the foreign key value. Load parent tables before child tables.

title: A parent row cannot be deleted because a foreign key relationship restricts the deletion
cause: Child rows still reference the parent row and the constraint uses ON DELETE RESTRICT or NO ACTION.
fix: Delete or re-point the child rows first, or define the constraint with ON DELETE CASCADE if that matches the business rule.

title: The requested operation is not allowed because a row does not satisfy a check constraint
cause: An inserted or updated row violates a CHECK constraint defined on the table.
fix: Read the constraint definition and correct the data.
example_sql: SELECT CONSTNAME, TEXT FROM SYSCAT.CHECKS WHERE TABSCHEMA = ? AND TABNAME = ?

title: The authorization ID does not have the privilege to perform the operation on the object
cause: The connected user lacks the required privilege (SELECT, INSERT, EXECUTE and so on) on the named object.
fix: Have the owner or a security administrator GRANT the specific privilege needed. Grant the minimum privilege, not DBADM.
example_sql: SELECT GRANTEE, SELECTAUTH, INSERTAUTH, UPDATEAUTH, DELETEAUTH FROM SYSCAT.TABAUTH WHERE TABSCHEMA = ? AND TABNAME = ?

title: The name of the object to be created is identical to an existing name
cause: A CREATE statement names an object that already exists in that schema.
fix: Use CREATE OR REPLACE where supported, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, drop the old object, or choose another name.

title: A duplicate column name was detected
cause: The same column name appears twice in a CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, view definition or INSERT column list.
fix: Remove or rename the duplicate. In views over joins, alias columns that share a name.

title: Operation not allowed on the table for the given reason code
cause: The table is in a restricted state. Reason code 7 means reorg pending after certain ALTER TABLE statements; reason code 1 means set integrity pending; reason code 3 means a failed LOAD left the table in load pending state.
fix: For reason code 7 run REORG TABLE. For reason code 1 run SET INTEGRITY ... IMMEDIATE CHECKED. For reason code 3 restart or terminate the LOAD.

title: Division by zero was attempted
cause: An arithmetic expression divided by a column or expression that evaluated to zero.
fix: Guard the divisor with NULLIF(divisor, 0) or a CASE expression.

title: One or more values are not valid because the primary key, unique constraint or unique index would have duplicate values
cause: An INSERT or UPDATE produces a key value that already exists. A common cause is an identity column whose next value is behind the data after a load or import.
fix: Find the duplicate key and correct the data, use MERGE for upserts, or restart the identity column above the current maximum with ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... RESTART WITH.
example_sql: SELECT INDNAME, COLNAMES FROM SYSCAT.INDEXES WHERE TABSCHEMA = ? AND TABNAME = ? AND UNIQUERULE IN ('P','U')

title: The result of a scalar fullselect, SELECT INTO or VALUES INTO is more than one row
cause: A subquery used where one value is expected returned several rows.
fix: Tighten the predicate so it is unique, add FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY with an ORDER BY, use an aggregate, or switch from = to IN.

title: The current transaction has been rolled back because of a deadlock or timeout
cause: Reason code 2 is a deadlock between transactions; reason code 68 is a lock timeout. The whole unit of work was rolled back.
fix: Retry the transaction. Keep transactions short, commit often, access tables in a consistent order, add indexes so fewer rows are locked, and review LOCKTIMEOUT and the isolation level.

title: Unsuccessful execution caused by deadlock or timeout
cause: The statement failed on a lock conflict but, unlike SQL0911N, the unit of work was not rolled back.
fix: Retry the statement or roll back explicitly. Apply the same lock-reduction steps as for SQL0911N.

title: Processing was cancelled due to an interrupt
cause: The statement was interrupted by the client: a query timeout, a cancelled request or the user pressing Ctrl+C.
fix: Raise the client query timeout if the statement is expected to run long, or tune the query so it finishes sooner.

title: The transaction log for the database is full
cause: A single unit of work, or the oldest uncommitted transaction, is holding more active log space than the database is configured for.
fix: Commit more frequently and break large DELETE or UPDATE jobs into batches. Find the application holding the oldest log record, then increase LOGFILSIZ, LOGPRIMARY or LOGSECOND if the workload needs it.

title: The database alias name or database name could not be found
cause: The database name in the connection is not catalogued on this client or does not exist on the server.
fix: Check the DATABASE value for typos, list the catalogued databases, and catalog the node and database if connecting remotely.

title: A database connection does not exist
cause: A statement was issued without an active connection, or the connection was dropped or closed earlier.
fix: Connect before executing, check for a failed earlier CONNECT, and add reconnect logic for long-lived applications.

title: The operation failed because the specified database cannot be connected to in the mode requested
cause: The database is in use by other connections and the operation needs exclusive access, or another application holds it exclusively.
fix: Wait, or disconnect other applications (FORCE APPLICATION) or QUIESCE the database before retrying an exclusive operation.

title: A connection to or activation of the database cannot be made because of BACKUP PENDING
cause: Archive logging was just enabled (LOGARCHMETH1 changed), so Db2 requires a full offline backup before the database can be used.
fix: Take a full offline backup of the database, then connect again.

title: There are no pages currently available in the buffer pool
cause: All pages in the buffer pool are in use and none can be stolen, typically because the buffer pool is too small for the concurrent workload.
fix: Increase the buffer pool size with ALTER BUFFERPOOL or set it to AUTOMATIC, and commit so pages are released.
example_sql: SELECT BPNAME, NPAGES, PAGESIZE FROM SYSCAT.BUFFERPOOLS

title: The database manager is not able to accept new requests, has terminated all requests in progress, or has terminated the specified request
cause: The instance is not started, the application was forced off, or an agent ended abnormally.
fix: Start the instance with db2start, check that the container or service is running, reconnect, and review db2diag.log if it recurs.

title: A temporary table space with sufficient page size does not exist
cause: A sort, join or wide result row needs a system temporary table space with a larger page size than any that exists.
fix: Create a buffer pool and a SYSTEM TEMPORARY table space with a 32K page size.
example_sql: SELECT TBSPACE, PAGESIZE, DATATYPE FROM SYSCAT.TABLESPACES

title: A communication error has been detected
cause: The client could not reach the server: wrong host or port, the instance or container is not running, a firewall blocks the port, or TLS settings do not match.
fix: Check HOSTNAME and PORT, confirm the instance is up and listening (DB2COMM=TCPIP, SVCENAME), test the port from the client, and match the SSL settings on both sides.

title: Security processing failed
cause: Authentication was rejected. Reason 24 is user ID or password invalid; reason 1 is password expired; reason 19 is user ID disabled or restricted.
fix: Re-enter the credentials, reset an expired password, and check that the user exists on the server operating system or the configured authentication plug-in.
